blocks.explanation:
All four angles are odd multiples of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) plus or minus \(\theta\), so every ratio changes to its co-ratio.
We must show the expression equals \(-1\).
Plan: reduce the four ratios, then use \(\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - \cot^2\theta = 1\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \sec\left(\frac{3\pi}{2} - \theta\right)\sec\left(\frac{5\pi}{2} - \theta\right) - \tan\left(\frac{3\pi}{2} - \theta\right)\tan\left(\frac{5\pi}{2} + \theta\right)\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= -1\).
Method: \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) and \(\frac{5\pi}{2}\) are odd multiples of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\): sec changes to cosec, tan changes to cot; the sign comes from the quadrant (\(\frac{5\pi}{2} = 2\pi + \frac{\pi}{2}\)).

Reduce the two secants
\[\sec\left(\tfrac{3\pi}{2} - \theta\right) = -\operatorname{cosec}\theta\]
\[\sec\left(\tfrac{5\pi}{2} - \theta\right) = \operatorname{cosec}\theta\]
Why: \(\frac{3\pi}{2} - \theta\) is in quadrant III, where cos (so sec) is negative. \(\frac{5\pi}{2} - \theta\) is one full turn plus \(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\), in quadrant I, so positive.

Reduce the two tangents
\[\tan\left(\tfrac{3\pi}{2} - \theta\right) = \cot\theta\]
\[\tan\left(\tfrac{5\pi}{2} + \theta\right) = -\cot\theta\]
Why: Quadrant III makes tan positive. \(\frac{5\pi}{2} + \theta\) is one full turn plus \(\frac{\pi}{2} + \theta\), in quadrant II, where tan is negative.

Substitute
\[\text{L.H.S.} = (-\operatorname{cosec}\theta)(\operatorname{cosec}\theta)\]
\[\quad - (\cot\theta)(-\cot\theta)\]
\[= -\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta + \cot^2\theta\]
Why: Minus times minus in the second term gives plus.

Use a Pythagorean identity
\[= -(\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - \cot^2\theta)\]
\[= -1 = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: \(1 + \cot^2\theta = \operatorname{cosec}^2\theta\), so \(\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - \cot^2\theta = 1\).
